title: Data Quality Tests & Incremental Loads
summary: Treat data like code: assert what must be true on every load (unique keys, no nulls, valid values, referential integrity), and process only what changed using a watermark.
takeaways: Data tests are assertions that run on every load and stop bad data before it reaches dashboards or models.
The core four: not_null, unique, accepted_values and relationships (referential integrity).
Use severities: an error blocks the pipeline, a warning alerts a human and lets the load continue.
Incremental loads process rows newer than a stored watermark, then advance it.

steps.label: Read watermark
steps.detail: Look up the max updated_at from the last successful run (none on the first run).

steps.label: Select new rows
steps.detail: Take only rows with updated_at greater than the watermark.

steps.label: Run data tests
steps.detail: not_null, unique, accepted_values, relationships, range: each with a severity.

steps.label: Gate
steps.detail: Any error-severity failure stops the load. Warnings are reported.

steps.label: Load + advance
steps.detail: Upsert the batch, then store the new watermark only after success.

terms.definition: An assertion about data (e.g. order_id is unique) that is evaluated automatically and fails when violated.
Every foreign-key value in a child table exists as a key in its parent table.
An explicit agreement on a dataset's schema and quality guarantees between producer and consumers.
The high-water mark (e.g. max updated_at) of data already processed, used to pick up only newer records.
A table built by processing only new or changed source rows on each run instead of rebuilding everything.
